Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Capital Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Capital Partners' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Reynolds, Chief Investment Officer; and Taylor Brooks, Head of Distribution.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional fund performance across our strategies and robust client inflows. Our AUM grew to $1.45 trillion.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. From a financial perspective, Apex Capital Partners delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $3.15 billion, representing a 13% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by the significant expansion in our assets under management and its direct translation to higher fee income. Our expenses were $2.1 billion, resulting in net income of $780 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently.

Let me elaborate on how AUM fluctuations profoundly shape our revenue profile. With ending AUM at $1.45 trillion, up 11% from the prior quarter and 17% year-over-year, our business model hinges on management fees, which made up about 92% of total revenues this period, alongside performance fees and ancillary income. This uptick stemmed from $110 billion in market gains, representing 73% of the rise, $34 billion in strong organic net inflows at 24%, and minor FX effects from our 27% non-USD assets.

Average daily AUM hit $1.41 trillion, up 9% sequentially, serving as the foundation for daily-accrued fees. Excluding a $50 million performance fee adjustment from our marquee long-short equity hedge fund, core management fees climbed 10%, tied almost wholly to AUM momentum. Our blended fee rate held at 43 basis points, off 1 bp due to pressures in passive ETFs. This implies a $6.2 billion annualized revenue run-rate, where each $100 billion AUM lift adds roughly $430 million yearly in fees. The quarter's AUM surge alone boosted the top line by $290 million, after fee adjustments.

By asset class, equities at 53% of AUM or $768 billion jumped 14% quarter-on-quarter amid S&P 500 and global index rallies, adding $215 million in fees, with active strategies like our Global Alpha Fund drawing inflows on quality growth bets in AI themes. Fixed income AUM of $425 billion eased 2% on yield spikes—the 10-year Treasury to 4.35%—causing $14 billion in valuation hits and some duration outflows, trimming blended fees slightly via lower-margin bond products. Alternatives, 19% or $276 billion, expanded 15% on $20 billion institutional commitments to private credit and infrastructure, yielding $130 million in performance fees from realizations, mirroring private market surges at firms like KKR.

Regionally, Americas at 63% or $1.09 trillion saw $24 billion inflows, powering 14% fee growth through retail via Schwab and Fidelity, plus DC plans favoring our target-date offerings. EMEA's $320 billion held steady against MiFID II hurdles but gained €16 billion in Nordic pensions for sustainable alts, upping fees 6%. APAC's $230 billion grew 19% via Sumitomo Mitsui partnerships, adding $90 million from Samurai bonds and China strategies despite tensions.

Organic flows at 2.4% annualized beat industry norms per Morningstar, aided by 66% retention, though fee erosion—down 19 bps over three years in passives—presses margins. Redemptions in duration-heavy bonds totaled $9 billion, echoing sector challenges.

We're countering with digital upgrades like our Aladdin 2.0 risk tool, cutting churn 16% and boosting flows 6%; new active ETFs including ESG small-cap at 26 bps fees, pulling $4.5 billion quickly; quant boutique integration for stable alpha; and scale with top clients at 53 bps fees.

Overall, AUM dynamics fuel our revenue engine, with H2 guidance for 9-11% growth implying high-teens top-line expansion.

Mike Reynolds: Thank you, Maria. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing quant-enhanced active management and thematic tilts. We launched our AI Infrastructure Fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $5 billion in commitments already.

Taylor Brooks: Thank you, Mike. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our active equity funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by diversified channel net flows totaling $16 billion, with institutional leading at $10.7 billion or 67%, up 32% year-over-year.

Institutional remains core, with 13-year average tenure. Pensions re-risked into our LDI solutions amid Fed and ECB shifts, $4.5 billion to core fixed income like Apex LDI Core Plus at $155 billion. North America 56% of flows on corporate cash to short credit; EMEA $4 billion on UK gilts and Nordic ESG infra; APAC $1.6 billion via multi-asset credit. Model portfolio APIs with Aladdin and Charles River sped RFPs 42%. New private credit interval fund seeded $2.2 billion for $1.6 trillion dry powder.

Retail $2.6 billion or 16%, off Q2 peak on seasonality but solid via ETFs capturing 13% active equity share. $1.3 billion equities led by Dividend Aristocrats ETF on yield chase; $950 million fixed via TDFs at $125 billion retirement AUM. US 72%, Europe $550 million on UCITS ESG, APAC $220 million countered by new ETF. Advisor portal AI tools upped SMA flows 27%.

Alternatives $2.7 billion, 17% mix up 42% YoY on illiquids for diversification. Private equity/credit $1.5 billion including Direct Lending Fund V at 11-13% IRR; real assets $950 million on IRA infra. North America 61%, EMEA 24%, APAC 15%. Semi-liquid REIT interval $350 million debut. Blended fees 96 bps.

Balanced flows set 7-9% AUM compounding.

Alex Rivera: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes ramping up technology and digital platform investments, where we committed $195 million in 2023, up 27% year-over-year or 12% of opex, matching leaders and yielding 23% digital AUM lift or $15 billion inflows, plus 16-point NPS rise to 79.

Client platforms like ApexOne, cloud-rebuilt on AWS with Bloomberg feeds, use AI for personalized recs; robo-hybrid holds 19% HNW share, $44 billion up 33%, with voice trades and ESG NLP at 73% adoption. Institutional risk platform with BlackRock cuts rebalancing to 12 minutes, ops costs 18%, averted $2.5 billion Q4 risks.

Tokenization pilots on Ethereum with State Street tokenized $550 million private credit for T+1 and 25% custody savings; AlphaGen AI adds 13 bps quant alpha; $30 million zero-trust cyber post-ION. APAC WeChat up 46% AUM $8.5 billion; EMEA RegTech saves 20% compliance, $7 billion SWF wins; Americas RIA APIs grow $115 billion.

$230 million 2024 capex for genAI and quantum security targets $17 trillion hybrid shift. Digital revenue $340 million up 42%, 9% total. This moat redefines our edge.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with Morningstar.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on fund performance relative to peers and benchmarks?

Alex Rivera: Great question, Sarah. I'll turn this over to our Chief Investment Officer, Mike Reynolds, for the rundown.

Mike Reynolds: Thanks, Alex, and good morning, Sarah. We're pleased our funds are providing superior risk-adjusted returns, surpassing benchmarks and peers in major strategies. Here's the breakdown: high-level, then asset classes, regions, and our advantages.

Q3-end AUM $1.45 trillion, +13% YoY on $19 billion inflows and $13 billion appreciation. Blended long-term composite 11.5% trailing 12-month net, vs. Morningstar Moderate Target Risk 10.1%, peer median 9.0% per Lipper on 1,300 funds.

Equities: Global Equity Fund GHGLX $47 billion, TER 0.67%, 15.7% YTD beating MSCI World 330 bps; 3-year 12.4% vs. 10.0%, top decile Lipper 460 large-blend. US Large-Cap Growth GHUSX 23.0% YTD +470 bps Russell 1000 Growth on Nvidia/Broadcom (190 bps alpha). Small-Cap Value 9.2% YTD +130 bps Russell 2000 Value, top-quartile vs. Vanguard/Fidelity, info ratio 0.67 in industrials/financials.

Fixed/multi: Strategic Bond GHSBX $34 billion 6.5% YTD +120 bps Bloomberg Agg via barbell—46% short IG 5.2% yield, 26% HY 8.4%; 5-year 4.3% vs. 2.5%, top-quintile intermediate core-plus. Multi-Asset Income GHMAX 10.1% YTD +250 bps 60/40 benchmark, beating PIMCO peers.

Alts/ESG: Global Real Assets +7.3% YTD +160 bps NCREIF on logistics/data centers. Private credit $16 billion 11.5% net IRR vs. Cliffwater 10.1%. Sustainable Equity GHESX 14.5% YTD matching MSCI ESG Leaders, top-decile vs. BlackRock ESGU via AI ESG scoring 15,000 issuers, Scope 3—100 bps excess.

Regions: NA 61% outperformance on tech; Europe Pan-European -40 bps YTD STOXX 600 on energy but 3-year +220 bps staples; APAC ex-JP 16.8% +390 bps MSCI AC Asia ex-JP on TSMC/China pivot. EM GHEMX 14.1% +430 bps MSCI EM, Mexico/India 26% nearshoring, Sharpe 1.15 vs. peer 0.87.

Trends: 150 bps avg alpha YTD, beta 0.97, -4.0% Aug drawdown vs. S&P -6.3%, Sharpe 1.07 vs. peers 0.94. 93% beat benchmarks 10-year Morningstar.

Edge: Horizon Alpha Engine ML on alt data—satellite/NLP—+80 bps small-cap Q3. TER down 6 bps to 0.51%. Thematic AI Infra Fund Q4 seed $5.5 billion tracks Indxx AI but 22% active. Model portfolios Schwab/Fidelity $3 billion RIA flows.

Forward: Fed 80 bps cuts aid bonds/cyclicals; risks geopolitics/China hedged 4.5% cash/VIX. Prioritize alpha, top-quartile.

Happy for follow-ups, Sarah.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. And a follow-up on distribution partnerships and channel expansion?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Sarah. Distribution partnerships and channel expansion are pivotal, fueling 47% of our $5.2 billion Q3 inflows. Amid $130 billion industry flows per ICI, we grabbed 4.2% active equity share.

RIA channel now 29% of $460 billion AUM, up from 19% in 18 months. Envestnet model marketplace added 13 SMA sleeves in Core Equity/Sustainable Growth with UMA tax harvesting via Alpha engine—$1.3 billion Q3 flows at 64 bps, resilient vs. industry 69 bps.

LPL sub-advisory for Dividend Aristocrats ETF ADIV: $900 million 90-day, 16% MoM growth post-Independence. Morgan Stanley E*TRADE: $700 million active ETFs like Global Thematic AGTM +23% YTD vs. MSCI Thematic 19%, API WealthPilot.

Taylor Brooks: Alex, to add metrics: Q3 inflows channel breakdown—RIAs $1.95 billion 37% +65% YoY 61 bps; BDs $1.2 billion 23% +48% 57 bps; wirehouses $1 billion 19% +34% 54 bps; direct/IBDs $0.55 billion 11% +23% 47 bps; inst/others $0.5 billion 10% +18% 41 bps. Total $5.2 billion +58% YoY blended 56 bps.

70% organic, ETFs 26% AUM $120 billion took 62% flows vs. EPFR 87% industry. Cost-to-serve RIAs down 13% to $440/$1M AUM via Salesforce.

Alex Rivera: Ahead on consolidation—LPL +9% advisors, Schwab synergies. $27 million tech: API Orion/Black Diamond direct indexing tax-alpha 130 bps; Vestmark/SEI OCIO for $2.1T RIA 13% CAGR Cerulli.

Europe BNP Paribas €1.3 billion ($1.4B) UCITS Euro Equity PRIIPs. Asia DBS Vickers Asia Growth ETF $450 million Singapore pool ex-China. LatAm Itaú Brazil $350 million EM pensions.

Robo/Vanguard squeeze betas, but 66% active top-quartile 82% Lipper; ESG Leaders +37% RIA. $16.5 billion pipeline 62% probable, RIAs/ETFs; 32% AUM new channels YE2025, 22-27 bps fee lift.

Covers it?

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with Bloomberg.

David Patel: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Global Equity Fund GHGLX?

Mike Reynolds: Good morning, David. Building on my earlier comments, GHGLX exemplifies our edge. At $47 billion, it posted 15.7% YTD through Q3, +330 bps over MSCI World, thanks to disciplined positioning in high-conviction names amid volatility. Three-year annualized 12.4% vs. benchmark 10.0%, landing top decile in Lipper's large-cap blend group of 460 funds. Our overweight in resilient growth sectors like tech and semis, combined with the Horizon Alpha Engine's alt data insights, generated meaningful alpha while keeping tracking error low at 2.2%. Peers struggled more with rotation risks, but our factor tilts delivered a Sharpe of 1.18. We're maintaining conviction here as global reacceleration supports the strategy.

David Patel: And how is the new product, the AI Infrastructure Fund, performing relative to expectations?

Taylor Brooks: Great question, David. The AI Infrastructure Fund has exceeded early expectations since launch, securing $5.5 billion in commitments within weeks, primarily from institutional and RIA channels. Initial allocations mirror the Indxx Global AI Infrastructure Index but with a 22% active overlay targeting semis, cloud computing, and power infrastructure—areas poised for multi-year growth. Performance net of fees is tracking +5% since inception against the index's +3.8%, driven by picks in power grid enablers amid data center buildouts. Distribution partnerships accelerated uptake, with Envestnet and LPL driving 40% of flows. We're on pace for $10 billion AUM by year-end, positioning it as a flagship thematic vehicle with resilient 55 bps fees.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Capital Partners. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
